title: Hyperspectral inversion model of ginkgo leaf yield prediction based on machine learning.
summary: Airborne hyperspectral measurements were used to estimate ginkgo leaf yield in field cultivation. The best reported combination, using PSAMA-selected spectral bands, vegetation indices and a BiLSTM with grid search, achieved Rp² 0.8795 and RMSEP 0.1021; the SNV-PLSR baseline achieved Rp² 0.7831 and RMSEP 0.0325. This is a field-yield prediction result, not evidence of transfer across sites or seasons.
ai_technology: Particle Swarm Attention Mechanism feature selection with BiLSTM grid-search regression

evidence.tested: Hyperspectral reflectance and selected vegetation indices were used to predict measured ginkgo leaf yield. The paper compares preprocessing and feature-selection/model combinations; the best reported combination is PSAMA with BiLSTM-GS (Rp² 0.8795, RMSEP 0.1021).
evidence.unknown: The reviewed result is from the study’s field data; performance across other sites, seasons or cultivars is not established.
evidence.ai_role: Learned spectral regression models predicted ginkgo leaf yield from airborne hyperspectral features; PSAMA selected bands and the BiLSTM-GS model estimated yield.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
